akhfash:1-1.t: He said: ﴿طه﴾. Some of them claim that it is two letters, like ﴿حَمّ] and some of them say {طه﴾ means "O man" in one of the dialects of the Arabs. «[Translator's note: the brackets in the source are mismatched; the text is reproduced as written.]»

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ﴾ as a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿لِتَشْقَىٰ﴾ [2], so he made it "We did not send down the Quran upon you except as a reminder".

akhfash:4-4.t: And He said ﴿تَنزِيلاً﴾, i.e. Allah sent that down as a sending-down (تنزيلا).

akhfash:5-5.t:
And He said ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ﴾, i.e. "He is the Most Merciful". Some read ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾, i.e. "a sending-down from the Most Merciful".
And He said ﴿عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ﴾: He means "عَلاَ" (He rose above), and the meaning of "عَلاَ" is "He had power (قَدَر)". He never ceased to be powerful, but He informed of His power.

akhfash:18-18.t: And He said ﴿مَآرِبُ أُخْرَىٰ﴾: its singular is "مَأْرُبَةٌ" (need).

akhfash:22-22.t: And He said ﴿آيَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾, i.e. "it brought out another sign", and he made it a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿بَيْضَآءَ﴾.

akhfash:42-42.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ تَنِيَا﴾: it is from "وَنَى" and "يَنِي", "وَنْياً" and "وُنِيّاً" (to slacken).

akhfash:44-44.t: And He said ﴿لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ﴾, like a man's saying to his companion: "افرَعْ لَعَلَّنَا نَتَغَدّى" (finish, perhaps we may have lunch), the meaning being: "so that we may have lunch" and "until we have lunch". And you say to a man: "اِعْمَلْ عَمَلَكَ لَعَلَّكَ تَأْخُذُ أَجْرَكَ" (do your work, perhaps you will take your wage), i.e. so that you may take it.

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿أَزْوَاجاً مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ﴾: He means "diverse pairs (أَزْواجاً شَتَّى) of plants"; or it is the plants that are diverse. All of that is sound.

akhfash:63-63.t:
And He said ﴿إِنْ هَـٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ﴾: light (إنْ) in the meaning of the heavy one (إنّ). It is the dialect of a people who use the nominative (after it) and bring in the lām to distinguish it from the one that has the meaning of "ما" (not). We read it heavy, and that is a dialect of the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.
And He said ﴿ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ﴾: the feminine of "الأَمْثَل" (the best), like "القُصْوَى" and "ألأَقْصَى" (the farthest).

akhfash:69-69.t: And He said ﴿ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ﴾; in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿أيْنَ أَتَى﴾. The Arabs say: "جِئْتُكَ من أيْنَ لا تَعْلَم" and "مِنْ حَيْثُ لا تَعْلَم" (I came to you from where you do not know).

akhfash:72-72.t: And He said ﴿لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَا﴾: He means "we will not prefer you over the One who created us".

akhfash:77-77.t: And He said ﴿لاَّ تَخَافُ دَرَكاً﴾, i.e. ﴿اِضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَريقا﴾ (strike for them a path) ﴿لاَّ تَخَافُ﴾ in it ﴿دَرَكاً﴾ (being overtaken). He omitted "فيه" (in it), just as you say: "زيدٌ أَكْرَمْتُ" (Zayd, I honoured), meaning "أَكْرَمْتُهُ" (I honoured him), and as He said ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئاً﴾, i.e. in which (a soul) will not avail.

akhfash:81-81.t: And He said ﴿فَيَحِلَّ﴾ and explained it as "يَجِب" (become due). Some read ﴿يَحُلَّ﴾ in the sense of "alighting", so they used ḍamma. And he said ﴿يَصِدُّونَ﴾ in the sense of "يَضِجُّونَ" (they clamour), and I consider it nothing but a dialect variant, like "يَعْكِفُ" and "ويَعْكُف", in the meaning of "يَصدّ". «[Translator's note: ﴿يَصِدُّونَ﴾ is from Q 43:57, not this verse; it appears here as written in the source.]»

akhfash:111-111.t: And He said ﴿وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ﴾: one says "عَنَتْ" "تَعْنُو" "عُنُوّاً" (to be humbled).

akhfash:129-129.t: And He said ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَاماً﴾: He means "and were it not for a word and ﴿أَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى﴾ (a stated term), it would have been inevitable".

akhfash:132-132.t: And He said ﴿لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾: for the people of taqwā (God-consciousness). In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وإِنْ العاقِبَةَ لِلتَّقْوى﴾.
